findings.element: The horizon's ceremonial date (.b-when) inside the 344px left column at 1024 and above
findings.problem: The left column is pinned at 344px for every desk width ([data-medium="full"] .b-two { grid-template-columns: 344px minmax(0,1fr) }, with .b-todayRule { max-width: 344px } to match). Driven at 1440x960 the fixture's own date, "Saturday 3 October 2026", inks 329.7px — 14px of slack. Every other plausible wedding date I typed into it wraps to two lines at 1024, 1152 AND 1440: "Saturday 12 September 2026", "Saturday 20 December 2025", "Wednesday 5 August 2026" all measure 78px tall instead of 39px. And they break in the worst possible place — the render is "Saturday 12" / "September 2026", splitting the day number from its month, on the single most emotional string in the product. So the composition is tuned to exactly one string; the gate's "no date breaks in half" passes because that string was the one chosen. Meanwhile the column beside it is 668px wide at 1440 carrying a longest line of 306px, so 350px of the measure column's right edge is permanently empty. The page's protagonist is the narrowest object on the page, and its slack was given to the column that had nothing to do with it.
findings.fix: Take the width from the column that is not using it. At the 1024 breakpoint set [data-medium="full"] .b-two { grid-template-columns: 420px minmax(0, 1fr) } and .b-todayRule { max-width: 420px } (the same 420 for [data-medium="full"] .b-press), which holds "Saturday 12 September 2026" on one line and costs the measure column 76px of the 350px it never draws in. Then make the remaining wrap survivable: in fixture.js's ceremonial-date formatter join the day number and the month name with U+00A0, so the only break the string permits is after the weekday — "Saturday" / "12 September 2026", never "Saturday 12" / "September 2026".

findings.element: The docked editing sheet (.b-edit) between 701px and 1023px
findings.problem: Round 7 capped the sheet's contents to a 480px measure but left the plate full-bleed (.b-edit { left: 12px; right: 12px }) and the contents flush to the plate's own 17px inset, so the measure was placed on nothing. Driven at 1023x900 with a moment open: the plate runs 12 to 1011, every field, label, stepper and button starts at x=29, and 500px of plate — half of it — is empty. The page's own content column starts at x=96 and the row titles above the sheet start at x=220, so the editor's fields sit 67px left of the left edge of everything they are editing. Two stacked objects on one screen disagreeing about where the page starts. At 900x800 it is the same picture with 380px of empty plate; at 768 with 240px. No frame in shots/ shows the docked sheet at any width — owner-editing is captured only at 1440 — so this is the classic undesigned edge, in the band the lessons file names by number.
findings.fix: Size the plate to the measure it already declares, and centre it on the page's axis (the stage is viewport-centred at these widths, so centring the plate lands it on the content column). In the docked branch of b.css add: .b-edit { left: 50%; right: auto; transform: translateX(-50%); width: min(514px, calc(100vw - 24px)); } and apply the same left/right/transform/width to the [data-undo="true"] .b-undoHome .b-undo rule beneath it so the reversibility bar stays flush with the sheet above it. Keep .b-edit > * { max-width: 480px } as the inner belt. The sheet then reads as one object with no half-empty plate, and its fields sit on the page's own axis instead of 67px outside it.

findings.element: The editing panel's reserved band — .b-edit { padding-top: 88px } and 104px under the coarse-pointer rule — with .b-edit .b-undo[data-empty="true"] hidden
findings.problem: The reserve itself is right and the round-7 refutation of moving it to the foot stands; what is wrong is that the reserve is blank. Measured at 1023 the panel's first label sits 89px below the panel's own top edge with nothing at all above it; on a phone the rule at line 1422 makes it 104px, inside a sheet that is already 559px of an 844px screen — 19% of the sheet, and 104px more of the plan pushed off the screen behind it. The panel also carries no visible heading of any kind: it names the moment it is editing only in the accessibility tree, so what a sighted owner sees on opening is a bordered plate with an empty top quarter and then a micro-label. It reads as a printing error, not as a held space, and it does that in every editing state at every width.
findings.fix:
Occupy the slot at rest with the panel's own heading, so the reserve is a design element rather than a hole and its height never changes. Render a first child in the panel,

Editing · Send the invitations

, carrying the same string the panel's aria-label already builds, and style it with exactly the geometry of the bar that replaces it: .b-editHead { position: absolute; top: 16px; left: 16px; right: 16px; min-height: 50px; padding: 0 0 var(--gap-snug); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--fore-16); font: 400 var(--size-micro)/var(--lead-body) var(--mono); letter-spacing: var(--track-micro); text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--fore-62); }. Hide it with visibility: hidden under the same selector that reveals the bar ([data-undo="true"] .b-edit .b-editHead), so exactly one of the two is drawn at all times and the 88/104px never moves.

findings.element: owner-empty — the first screen a new owner ever sees
findings.problem: Two placement faults on the one screen that has nothing else on it to look at. First, [data-medium="sheet"|"full"] .b-empty { padding: 110px 56px 120px } indents the only block on the page 56px from the page's own left margin while the bar above it and the foot below it sit on that margin: measured at 1440, the bar and foot start at x=186 and "When is the day?" starts at x=242; at 768 it is 96 against 152. Three objects, two left edges, and 1012px of empty ground to the right of the block at 1440. Second, shell.css gives min-height: 100dvh to publish, day, ended, loading and unfurl — the states it recognised as one object in a room — but not to owner-empty, so this page stops short of the window: the stage ends at 796.9 in a 960px viewport, at 649.7 in an 844px phone, leaving the footer hanging in mid-air with 163px and 194px of dead ground beneath it. The class was found and fixed for five states and missed on the sixth.
findings.fix: Change the rule to [data-medium="sheet"] .b-empty, [data-medium="full"] .b-empty { padding: 110px 0 120px } — the block already carries its own measure on .b-emptyTitle and .b-emptyBody, so nothing but the left edge moves, and the heading, body, field and hint then share the edge of the bar and the foot. Then add [data-state="owner-empty"] .tl-page to the min-height: 100dvh selector list in shell.css (line 246-249) so the foot lands on the bottom of the window exactly as it does in the five states already in that list.

findings.element: The hovered and being-edited row plate — box-shadow: 0 0 0 12px on .b-item .b-copy
findings.problem: The plate behind a row is painted as a 12px spread box-shadow rather than on the element, and .b-copy's right edge is exactly the page's content column: measured 370 at 390, 672 at 768, 1254 at 1440. So the plate paints to 382 / 684 / 1266 and is the only ink anywhere on the page that crosses the margin the header rule and the footer both stop on. On the left the 12px lands in the empty channel between the rail and the words and reads as intended; on the right it simply overhangs. While a moment is open that plate is the loudest object on the screen — in the 1440 owner-editing frame you can see its right edge standing proud of the rule above it — and on a phone it leaves 8px to the screen edge where every other object keeps 20. One broken edge on a page whose entire argument is measured alignment.
findings.fix: Paint the plate on the element instead of outside it. Add to the base rule: .b-item .b-copy { padding: 12px; margin: -12px 0 -12px -12px; border-radius: 16px; } and change the three plate rules — .b-item:hover .b-copy, .b-item:focus-within .b-copy and .b-item[data-editing="true"] .b-copy — from box-shadow: 0 0 0 12px <tint> to background: <tint> alone (keep the existing background declarations and the transition). The plate then runs from 12px left of the row's words to the column's right edge — 698 to 1254 at 1440 — the words gain a 12px right gutter they do not have today, and the page keeps one right margin. Leave the [data-crowded="true"] knockout shadow as it is; that one is a knockout, not a plate.

biggestWin: The horizon block, and the fact that it is a real protagonist rather than a big number. A 148px mono count pulled back -0.05em so the numeral's side bearing lands on the page's left edge instead of measuring to it; the ceremonial date, the day's name and one 344px indigo hairline stacked under it in a single descending rhythm; and at desk width the whole block sticking at the top of its own column and rewriting its own last line — "Nothing is planned until 1 August." becomes "8 August · 23 days away" — as the measure scrolls past it. The proportional measure beside it holds its side of the bargain: the vertical holes are real distance and they read as distance, not as loose spacing. Almost nothing on the surface is composed by default; the count, the rail, the two-column split at 1024, the phone stack and the printed sheet are each placed by a decision you can name. That is the part that is already at the standard, and it is why the remaining faults are placement in specific bands rather than anything structural.
